1) Aggrieved by the impugned Decree and Award, dated 05.03.2012, passed in M.V.O.P. No. 48 of 2008 on the file of the Motor Accidents Claims Tribunal-cum-District Judge, Kadapa at Proddatur,
whereby, the claim of Rs.3,66,000/- was awarded to the Claimants towards compensation, this Appeal is preferred by the Claimants claiming remaining balance compensation amount, as prayed in the claim petition.

entities.text: Motor Accidents Claims Tribunal-cum-District Judge, Kadapa at Proddatur
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: 2) For the sake of convenience, both the parties in the Appeal will be referred to as they are arrayed in the claim application.

3) The claim petitioners filed the petition under Section 166 of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 [the 'M.V. Act'], against the respondent claiming compensation of Rs.7,50,000/- for the death of one R.
Suryanarayana Reddy [the 'deceased'], in a motor vehicle accident that took place on 22.09.2007.

4) Facts germane to dispose of the Appeal may briefly be stated as follows: -
i. On 22.09.2007, the deceased proceeded from Kadapa to Nellore on his motorcycle bearing registration No.AP04 D 9140, and at about 5.00 P.M. when the deceased reached near Kadirinaidupalli Village on Badvel - Nellore main road, the respondent's A.P.S.R.T.C. bus bearing registration No.AP10 Z 9191 came in opposite direction, driven by its driver, in a rash and negligent manner without blowing horn,
dashed against the motorcycle of the deceased, as a result the deceased fell down and sustained head injury and died on the spot itself.
A case was registered against the driver of the offending A.P.S.R.T.C. bus.
5) The respondent filed written statement with a plea that the respondent is not liable to pay any compensation and the accident occurred due to rash and negligent act on the part of the deceased.

6) Based on the above pleadings, the following issues were settled for trial by the Tribunal:
(i) Whether the accident occurred on 22.09.2007 at about 5.00 P.M. due to rash and negligent driving of the driver of A.P.S.R.T.C. bus bearing No. AP10 Z 9191?

7)
During the course of enquiry, on behalf of the petitioners, PW1 and PW2 were examined and Ex.A1 to Ex.A9 were marked.
On behalf of the respondent, no witnesses were examined and no documents are marked.

8) At the culmination of the enquiry and on appreciation of the entire evidence available on record, the Tribunal awarded compensation of Rs.3,66,000/- towards total compensation to all the claimants.
Aggrieved thereby, the claimants preferred this instant appeal for claiming remaining balance of compensation amount, as prayed in the claim application.

9) Heard learned counsels for both the parties and perused the record.
10) Now, the point for determination is:
i) Whether the order of the Tribunal needs any interference of this Court?

If so, to what extent?
ii) Whether the appellants/claimants are entitled to remaining balance compensation amount, as prayed in the claim application?
11) POINT Nos. (i) & (ii): The 1st claimant is the wife of the deceased.

The case of the claimants is that, on 22.09.2007, the deceased [R.Suryanarayana Reddy] proceeded from Kadapa to Nellore on his motorcycle bearing registration No.AP04 D 9140, and at about 5.00 P.M. when the deceased reached near Kadirinaidupalli Village on Badvel - Nellore main road, the respondent's A.P.S.R.T.C. bus bearing registration No.AP10 Z 9191 came in opposite direction, driven by its driver, in a rash and negligent manner without blowing horn, dashed against the motorcycle of the deceased, as a result the deceased was thrown on the road and he sustained bleeding head injury and died at the spot itself.
12) In order to prove rash and negligent driving of the driver of the offending vehicle, the petitioners relied on the evidence of PW1 and PW2.
PW1 is not an eye witness to the incident.
PW2 is an eye witness to the incident.

The evidence of PW2 goes to show that the accident in question occurred due to rash and negligent driving of the driver of A.P.S.R.T.C. bus, in which the deceased sustained fatal injuries and died at the spot itself.
In cross-examination, nothing was elicited from PW2 to discredit the testimony of PW2.
The material on record reveals that the accident in question occurred due to rash and negligent driving on the part of the driver of the A.P.S.R.T.C. bus.
The Tribunal also came to the same conclusion.
I do not find any legal flaw or infirmity in the award given by the Tribunal.

sentences.text:
Coming to the compensation, the claimants are claiming compensation of Rs.7,50,000/-
towards total compensation.

The contention of the claimants is that, the deceased used to earn Rs.2,20,000/- per annum, but, in order to prove the same, no evidence is adduced by the claimants.
Therefore, on considering the entire evidence on record, since the accident occurred in the year 2007, the monthly income of the deceased was arrived at Rs.3,000/- per month [Rs.100/- per day]
and annual income as Rs.36,000/- per annum [Rs.3,000/- x 12].
The dependents on the deceased are four in number.

Therefore, as per the decision of Sarla Varma Vs. Delhi Transport Corporation1,
1/4th amount has to be deducted towards personal expenses of the deceased, but the Tribunal deducted 1/3rd of the personal expenses of the deceased, which is not sustainable under law.

entities.text: Sarla Varma Vs. Delhi Transport Corporation1
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: If 1/4th is deducted from out of Rs.36,000/-, an amount of Rs.27,000/- is available to the dependents [Rs.36,000/- - Rs.9,000/-].
The age of the deceased was 35 years and the relevant multiplier applicable to the age group of the deceased is "16".
Therefore, Rs. 4,32,000/- [Rs.27,000/- x 16] is awarded towards 'loss of dependency'.

As per the decision of National Insurance Company Limited Vs. Pranay 2009 (4) SCJ 91 Sethi2, an amount of Rs.40,000/- is awarded towards 'loss of consortium' to the 1st claimant; an amount of Rs.15,000/- is awarded towards 'loss of estate'; and Rs.15,000/- is awarded towards 'funeral expenses' of the deceased.

In total, a sum of Rs.5,02,000/-
is awarded towards compensation to the claimants.
14) In the result, the appeal is partly allowed.
The claim of Rs.3,66,000/- awarded by Tribunal is enhanced to Rs.5,02,000/-.

The claimants are entitled to enhanced compensation of Rs.1,36,000/-
with interest @ 6% per annum from the date of petition till the date of realization.
The respondent/A.P.S.R.T.C. is directed to deposit the enhanced compensation of Rs.1,36,000/- with interest at 6% per annum, as ordered above, within two months from the date of this judgment.
On such deposit, the claimants are entitled to withdraw the same along with interest therein equally.
The share of 2nd appellant/claimant shall be kept as fixed deposit in a nationalized bank until he attains majority.
On attaining majority, the 2nd 2017 (16) SCC 680 appellant/claimant is permitted to withdraw the same.
No order as to costs.
15) As a sequel, miscellaneous petitions, if any, pending in the Appeal shall stand closed.
